_meta.purpose: Demo seed data for the Greater Hartford pilot scene. Researched from public sources so the demo looks like the real Connecticut scene instead of a directory of invented names.
rules: DEMO AND LOCAL DEVELOPMENT ONLY. None of the real acts or venues listed here agreed to be on Riff; this file must never seed a public or production database (the seeders refuse production).
Entries with "real": true describe real acts/venues from public sources: factual third-person bios, public street addresses for public venues, and only music links verified during research.

Entries with "real": false are invented. Everything that attributes a state or action to its subject stays on fictional entries ONLY: hidden/archived profiles, seeded reports and the moderation queue, feed posts written in the artist's voice, listings, lineup slots shown as pending/declined, and cancelled shows.
Shows are plausible compositions (real bands at venues they could play, dated relative to seeding), not real events. Member accounts behind every act are invented.

No real DIY space is listed: a private venue's whole point is that Riff never holds its address, and outing one's existence is harm the privacy rules exist to prevent. The DIY space here is fictional.

Support links are on fictional entries ONLY. A support section is an invitation to pay, which is a stronger attribution than listing a link: Riff must not imply a real act asks for money anywhere. Real acts keep only their research-verified Bandcamp link, rendered as a link, not as a support ask. Seeded click counts are invented and exist to demo the counter.

acts.name: Boundaries
acts.bio: Metalcore out of Hartford, formed in 2015 and heavier with every record — Your Receding Warmth, Burying the Brightness, and Death Is Little More on Unbeaten Records.

acts.name: The Lonesome While
acts.bio: Hartford punk and indie rock. The Lost of Us (2025) collected a decade of songs that nearly stayed on the shelf — one of the city's underrated gems.

acts.name: Perennial
acts.bio: Art-punk three-piece — electric guitar, electric organ, drums — splitting the difference between mod pop, post-hardcore and 60s soul. A Stereogum Best New Artist of 2024; Modernism is the latest.

acts.name: West End Blend
acts.bio: Eight-piece funk and soul powerhouse from Hartford fronted by Erica T. Bryan — a Northeast club and festival staple for a decade.

acts.name: Joey Batts & Them
acts.bio: Alternative hip-hop with a live band, from Hartford. Joey Batts taught in Hartford public schools for years and runs Hip Hop for the Homeless, a statewide benefit tour, every December.

acts.name: Make Do and Mend
acts.bio: Melodic post-hardcore from West Hartford, active again after the long quiet stretch.

acts.name: Anxious
acts.bio: Melodic hardcore and emo from Fairfield County. The second LP, Bambi, came out on Run for Cover in February 2025.

acts.name: Cheem
acts.bio: Nu pop from nu England: Trumbull's own, splicing 2000s pop, metal and post-hardcore. Fast Fashion and Faster Fashion say it all.

acts.name: Ovlov
acts.bio: Fuzz-heavy indie rock from Newtown and a New England basement-show fixture for well over a decade.

acts.name: Hatebreed
acts.bio: The biggest name in Connecticut hardcore, out of Bridgeport and New Haven since 1994.

acts.name: The Meadows Brothers
acts.bio: Brothers Ian and Dustin Meadows out of Chester: homegrown, folked-up, countrified, rock-n-rolled roots music. In the Land of Steady Habits (2025) is the new one.

acts.name: Eggy
acts.bio: Four-piece jam band from New Haven — funk, psychedelic rock and blues, heavy on the live tapes.

acts.name: Residual Groove
acts.bio: Bridgeport jam-rock that has gigged every room in the state.

acts.name: The Silver Mill
acts.bio: Fast, short, loud. We book our own shows in basements and VFW halls and split the door evenly.

acts.name: Quiet Transit
acts.bio: Instrumental, loud at the end. We rehearse in a converted office above a print shop downtown.

acts.name: Marisol Vega
acts.bio: Singer and guitarist. I grew up between Hartford and Ponce and the songs come out somewhere in the middle.

acts.name: DJ Lowtide
acts.bio: Records every other Friday at a bar on Pratt Street. Mostly house, some disco, nothing before midnight.

acts.name: Thread City Ska
acts.bio: Eight of us, named for the mills. If there is a street festival within an hour of Willimantic, we have played it.

acts.name: Mirrorwork
acts.bio: Hardware techno made in a storage unit. Profile is here; the pin is not, by choice.

acts.name: Pale Lantern
acts.bio: Quiet band, slow songs. We keep a profile for bookings but we would rather not be a pin on a map.

acts.name: The Winter Ledger
acts.bio: On hold while two of us are out of state. Archived rather than deleted, which is the point of archiving.

venues.name: Arch Street Tavern
venues.description: Live music inside a turn-of-the-century carriage factory downtown — jam, funk and regional acts most weekends, with a full bar and kitchen.

venues.name: The Webster
venues.description: Hartford's enduring rock club: the main theater upstairs and the Underground downstairs for rising hardcore, metal, punk and hip-hop bills.

venues.name: Black-Eyed Sally's
venues.description: Blues, jazz and soul over barbecue — a downtown landmark and a regular stop on the Hip Hop for the Homeless tour.

venues.name: Real Art Ways
venues.description: Arts organization in Frog Hollow programming experimental and genre-crossing performance alongside film and galleries.

venues.name: Parkville Market
venues.description: Connecticut's first food hall, with live bands on the regular — Fiesta Fridays especially.

venues.name: Infinity Hall Hartford
venues.description: A roughly 500-cap room in the Front Street district with a famously good PA.

venues.name: Cafe Nine
venues.description: The musician's living room at State and Crown — local bills most nights of the week, still locally owned.

venues.name: Space Ballroom
venues.description: Hamden's mid-size independent room, splitting its calendar between touring indie acts and Connecticut bands.

venues.name: The Buttonwood Tree
venues.description: Community-run, not-for-profit listening room on Main Street — about fifty seats, folk and jazz on weekends, open mics on Mondays and Thursdays.

venues.name: Bridge Street Live
venues.description: Intimate room on the Farmington River for blues, folk and regional acts.

venues.name: Basement Signal
venues.description: A basement with a running calendar. Ask a punk for the address; be good to the neighbours.

venues.name: The Old Foundry
venues.description: Hasn't listed a show in over a year — off the map until it does, though its page is still here.

location.note: Ask a punk, or DM the band

location.label: Riverfront park bandshell
location.note: Rain moves it indoors — check back here

listings.title: Drummer wanted — fast, short, loud
listings.body: Our drummer moved to Philly. We play basements and VFW halls, practise Tuesdays in New Britain, and split everything evenly. Need someone who can hold 200bpm for 90 seconds at a time.

listings.title: Bassist looking for a band
listings.body: Fifteen years on bass, own amp and a car. Into post-punk, shoegaze, anything with a groove. Can do two nights a week around Hartford.

listings.title: Openers wanted for our spring shows
listings.body: Booking a run of all-ages shows in the spring and want local openers — ska, punk, reggae, anything with energy. Message us with a link to your music.

listings.title: Sharing our rehearsal room
listings.body: Soundproofed room above a print shop downtown, full backline. Free Mondays and Thursdays — looking for a band to split the rent.
